content.text: Plait Solitaire (also known as 'Plaits' or 'The Braid') is a double-deck solitaire game of significant complexity and visual appeal. It is distinguished by the 'Plait'â€”a central reserve of 13 cards arranged in a braid-like pattern, where only specific cards are accessible at any time. Requiring the player to manage two sets of foundations and eight tableau piles, it is a game of foresight, sequence planning, and careful reserve management.
Dates back to the mid-19th century as a complex 'Grand Patience' played in European parlors. The 'Plait' layout was designed to provide a decorative yet difficult reserve element.
One player. Plait is a solo patience game played by a single person; BVS and historical sources describe it as a single-player card game with no opponents or partners.

Deal 13 cards in a plait (open reserve). Deal 32 cards into 8 tableau piles (4 cards per pile). Place one card above as the first foundation base; the seven other cards of the same rank become foundation bases as they appear. Remainder is stock.

items.text: Standard: Standard Plait: 13-card plait reserve, 8 tableau piles (4 cards each), 8 foundations (one base rank revealed at start), remainder stock; build up in suit on foundations, down alternating color on tableau; no redeal.
Similar games: Braid, Cadonette and Fort are similar double-deck solitaires documented by BVS but are distinct games with their own rules.
Other variants: No other named variants for Plait Solitaire are documented in BVS or primary sources.
